macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Bitcoin and major cryptocurrencies remain under pressure
items.summary: Bitcoin was reported near $64,768, up 1.27% over 24 hours after recovering from a weekend drop toward $62,000. Ether was around $1,810, while market weakness has been linked to ETF outflows, high interest rates and leveraged liquidations.

items.title: Backpack receives CFTC approvals for blockchain-based derivatives exchange
items.summary: Backpack received approval for Designated Contract Market and Derivatives Clearing Organization licenses, positioning it to launch a U.S. blockchain-based derivatives exchange with round-the-clock trading and perpetual contracts.

items.title: Solana activates Alpenglow and moves to protocol version 1.0
items.summary: Solana reportedly ended Mainnet Beta and activated Alpenglow, a protocol upgrade intended to reduce transaction finality to roughly 150 milliseconds.

items.title: Kava’s HARD Lend exploited for about 53.9 million KAVA
items.summary: The Kava lending protocol suffered an exploit attributed to an accounting vulnerability. A separate attack on Lighter involving API-key nonce reuse reportedly led to the return of about 5 million USDC and resumed withdrawals.

items.title: South Korea moves against unregistered crypto exchanges
items.summary: South Korea’s Financial Intelligence Unit reportedly said websites for 27 unregistered exchanges, including KuCoin, MEXC, BitMart and BingX, would be blocked, while 44 firms were referred to investigators.

items.title: Hong Kong plans broader digital-asset licensing rules
items.summary: Hong Kong reportedly plans to submit legislation before year-end covering licensing for digital-asset trading, asset management and custody services.

items.title: Crypto holdings at South Korea’s largest exchanges decline
items.summary: Upbit and Bithumb saw their combined cryptocurrency holdings fall by 332.6 billion won amid the market slump. Bitcoin was trading around 88.34 million won on Upbit, down 0.21% from the prior day.

items.title: North Korea linked to $6 billion Binance crypto theft, report says
items.summary: The FBI reportedly attributed a $6 billion cryptocurrency theft from Binance to North Korea, with the incident contributing to a broader decline in crypto prices.

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: SiMa.ai releases Palette 3.0 for physical AI
items.summary: SiMa.ai announced Palette 3.0, a software release intended to improve performance and deployment across physical-AI models, including agentic applications.

items.title: Anthropic and Google announce new AI models
items.summary: Anthropic reportedly launched Claude Fable 5.1 and Claude Mythos 5.1, while Google announced Gemini 3.8 Flash and Gemini 3.8 Flash Cyber. The announcements emphasize coding, scientific research, cybersecurity, and lower-cost inference.

items.title: OpenAI Astra reaches critical cybersecurity capability tier
items.summary: OpenAI said its upcoming Astra model became the first to reach the company’s “Critical” cybersecurity capability tier, prompting debate over safety monitoring and reasoning transparency.

items.title: Shanghai AI Lab releases Sage S2.1 Flash
items.summary: Shanghai Artificial Intelligence Laboratory released Sage S2.1 Flash, a multimodal scientific model designed for iterative analysis, verification, retrieval, programming, and tool use.

items.title: LangChain raises $300 million for AI-agent platform
items.summary: LangChain reportedly raised $300 million at a $3 billion valuation, highlighting continued investor interest in infrastructure for deploying and operating AI agents.

items.title: Sarvam launches India-hosted inference platform
items.summary: Sarvam introduced Token Factory, an OpenAI-compatible inference service hosted in India and offering access to eight models on NVIDIA B200 clusters.

items.title: Liquid AI releases new decision models
items.summary: Liquid AI released d1.2 and d1.2-ultra, multimodal decision models supporting text, images, and audio; the company reported a leading score for d1.2-ultra on the Artificial Analysis Decision Index.

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: FaZe Esports wins Rainbow Six Osaka Major
items.summary: FaZe Esports swept DarkZero 3-0 to win the Rainbow Six Osaka Major and a $200,000 prize. The victory gives its roster major titles at the Six Invitational, Esports World Cup and BLAST R6 Major.[1]

items.title: Steam release-fee increase proposed amid submission surge
items.summary: Indie figures Mike Rose and Rami Ismail proposed raising Steam’s game submission fee to $2,500, arguing that the platform’s review process is struggling with a sharp rise in releases and AI-generated games.[4]

items.title: IEM Beijing to return through 2028
items.summary: ESL FACEIT Group and Beijing esports authorities signed a three-year agreement covering IEM Beijing events from 2026 through 2028, extending the city’s role on the Counter-Strike 2 calendar.[6]

items.title: Two games join Xbox Game Pass
items.summary: Sci-fi adventure Aphelion and family title PAW Patrol: Dino World became available to Xbox Game Pass subscribers.[8]

items.title: Hanwha Life Esports head coach departs
items.summary: Yoon Sung-young has left his position as head coach of Hanwha Life Esports, marking a notable coaching change in the competitive League of Legends scene.[2]

items.title: Grand Theft Auto VI launch hype intensifies
items.summary: Grand Theft Auto VI is scheduled to launch on November 19, with reports highlighting unusually high pre-release demand and expectations that its release could become a major cultural and commercial event.[3]
